notes.text: I will not — By asking a sign, as if I questioned the truth of his word: but this was deep hypocrisy.

David — He reproves them all, because they were the king's counsellors. Is it a small thing - Is it not wickedness enough. My God - To vex God's prophets and people, with your oppressions and horrid impieties. And by your ingratitude and unbelief, and disobedience of his commands.

Therefore — Because you despise me, and the sign which I now offer to you, God of his own free grace will send you a more honourable messenger, and give you a nobler sign. A sign - Of your deliverance. But how was this birth, which was not to happen 'till many ages after, a sign of their deliverance from present danger? This promised birth supposed the preservation of that city, and nation and tribe, in and of which the Messiah was to be born; and therefore there was no cause to fear that ruin which their enemies now threatened. Immanuel - God with us; God dwelling among us, in our nature, John i, 14. God and man meeting in one person, and being a mediator between God and men. For the design of these words is not so much to relate the name by which Christ should commonly he called, as to describe his nature and office.

glossa.text:
*Ask thee a sign.* ((ID.)) That he who did not believe the prophet might be terrified by the authority of the Lord; as if he should say: It seems hard to thee that most powerful kingdoms should be brought to an end in a short time, and that thou shouldst be delivered, and thy people; but ask thee a sign.

*Ask thee a sign.* Moses received a sign from the earth, etc., *as far as* it looks to both the death of the Lord and his ascension.

*I will not ask.* Not humbly, but proudly. For many are read to have asked signs of the Lord and to have received them; but Achaz answered thus, as having authority: *Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.* Or, he feared that in the sign God should be glorified and the idols made cheap.

*Behold a virgin shall conceive.* ((ID.)) In Hebrew *alma;* in Latin also *alma* is called holy, etc., *as far as* that it arose by violence is plain even to fools.

*Emmanuel.* ((ID.)) Some say that Isaias had two sons, etc., *as far as* for the sake of which the Word was made flesh.

notes.text: Enditing — Hebrew. boileth, or bubbleth up like water over the fire. This denotes that the workings of his heart, were fervent and vehement, kindled by God's grace, and the inspiration of the Holy Ghost. Made - Have composed. Pen - He was only the pen or instrument in uttering this song; it was the spirit of God, by whose hand this pen was guided.

Fairer — Than all other men: which is most true of Christ; but not of Solomon; whom many have excelled, in holiness and righteousness, which is the chief part of the beauty celebrated in this psalm. Grace - God hath plentifully poured into thy mind and tongue the gift of speaking wisely, eloquently, and acceptably. Therefore - And because God hath so eminently qualified thee for rule, therefore he hath blessed thee with an everlasting kingdom.
Thy sword — To smite thine enemies. And the sword is here put for all his arms, as it is in many other places.

And — Being thus magnificently girt and armed. Ride - March on speedily and successfully against thine enemies. The word - That is, the gospel: which is called the word of truth, Eph. i, 13, and may no less truly be called the word of meekness, because it is not delivered with terror, as the law was at Sinai, but meekly and sweetly; and the word of righteousness, because it brings in everlasting righteousness, and strongly excites all men to the practice of righteousness and holiness. And so the gospel is compared, to an horse or chariot, upon which Christ is said to ride, when the gospel is preached, and carried about from place to place. Teach thee - Thou shalt do exploits, which shall be terrible to thine enemies. But the phrase, thy right hand shall teach thee, is not to be taken properly; the meaning is, his hand should shew him, discover and work before him.

Arrows — The same with the sword, and this is no other than his word, which is sharp and powerful, and pierceth the hearts of men. The kings - Of thine enemies. Fall - Prostrate at thy feet, after the manner of conquered persons.

O God — It is evident, that the speech is still continued to the same person whom he calls king, ver. 1, 11, and here God, to assure us that he doth not speak of Solomon, but a far greater king, who is not only a man, but the mighty God, Isaiah ix, 6. A right scepter - Thou rulest with exact righteousness and equity.

Therefore — Therefore God hath exalted thee far above all men and angels, to a state of joy and endless glory at his right hand; which is fitly compared by the oil of gladness. Thy God - According to thy human nature, John xx, 17, though in respect of thy Divine nature, thou art his fellow, Zech xiii, 7, and his equal, Phil ii, 6, and one with him, John x, 30. Oil - So called, because it was a token of gladness, and used in feasts, and other solemn occasions of rejoicing. Fellows - Above all them who partake with thee in this unction: above all that ever were anointed for priests or prophets, or kings.

Myrrh — Wherewith they used to perfume their garments: this may denote those glorious and sweet smelling virtues, which, as they were treasured up in Christ's heart, so did they manifest themselves outwardly, and give forth a grateful smell, in the whole course of his life and actions. Palaces - The king is here supposed to reside in his ivory palaces, and his garments are so fragrant, that they not only perfume the whole palace in which he is; but the sweet favour is perceived by those that pass by them, all which is poetically said, and with allusion to Solomon's glorious garments and palaces. The heavenly mansions, may not unfitly be called ivory palaces, as elsewhere in the same figurative manner they are said to be adorned with gold and precious stones, from which mansions Christ came into the world, into which Christ went, and where he settled his abode after he went out of the world, and from whence he poured forth all the fragrant gifts and graces of his spirit, although there is no necessity to strain every particular circumstance in such poetical descriptions; for some expressions may be used, only as ornaments, as they are in parables; and it may suffice to know, that the excellencies of the king Christ are described by things which earthly potentates place their glory. Whereby - By the sweet smell of thy garments out of those ivory palaces, or the effusion of the gifts and graces of thy spirit from heaven; which as it is a great blessing to those who receive them, so doth it rejoice the heart of Christ, both as it is a demonstration of his own power and glory, and as it is the instrument of bringing souls to God. Made thee - Thou art made glad.

Among — Among them that attend upon thy spouse, as the manner was in nuptial solemnities. As the queen is the church in general, and so these honourable women are particular believers, who are daily added to the church, Acts ii, 47. And although the church is made up of particular believers, yet she is distinguished from them, for the decency of the parable. And these believers may be said to be Kings daughters, because among others, many persons of royal race embraced the faith, and because they are in a spiritual sense, Kings unto God, Rev. i, 6. Right hand - The most honourable place. Ophir - Clothed in garments made of the choicest gold. By which he designs the graces wherewith the church is accomplished.

Hearken — The prophet having hitherto spoken to the bridegroom, now addresseth his speech to the bride. O daughter - He speaks like an elder person, and as her spiritual father and counsellor. Incline - He uses several words, signifying the same thing, to shew his vehement desire of her good. Forget - Comparatively.
So — So thou shalt be acceptable to thy husband; which will abundantly recompence thee, for the loss of thy father's house. Thy Lord - As he is thy husband, and also as he is thy king, and God.

The daughter — The people of Tyre; as the daughter of Zion or Jerusalem, are put for their inhabitants: he mentions the Tyrians; because they among others, and before many others, were to be converted to Christ, but they are here put for all the Gentiles, whom that city fitly represents, as being the mart of the nations. A gift - To testify their homage. The rich - Of other nations.

Daughter — The spouse; so called, because she was the daughter of one king, and the wife of another. Within - In her soul. Her cloathing - She is outwardly adorned with virtuous and honourable actions.
Brought — He alludes to the custom of conducting the bride to the bride-groom's house. Companions - Her bride-maidens attending upon her.

Instead — Having directed his speech to the bride, he now returns to the bridegroom, as may be gathered both from the Hebrew words, which are of the masculine gender; and from the next verse, which unquestionably belongs unto him, and therefore this cannot be understood of Solomon, and his marriage with Pharaoh's daughter, because he had no children by her, and but very few by all his wives and concubines; and his children were so far from being made Princes in all the earth, that they enjoyed but a small part of their father's dominions, but this was fully accomplished in Christ: who instead of his fathers of the Jewish nation, had a numerous posterity of Christians of all the nations of the earth, which here and elsewhere are called princes and kings, because of their great power with God and with men.

Remembered — As he began the psalm with the celebration of the king's praises, so now he ends with it, and adds this important circumstance, that this nuptial song should not only serve for the present solemnity, but should be remembered and sung in all successive generations. The safety of the church under God's care, ver. 1-7. An exhortation to behold his works, and to trust in him, ver. 8-11. To the chief musician for the sons of Korah, A song upon Alamoth.

glossa.text:
*It hath uttered forth.* ((AUG., HIER.)) For the Prophet speaks within, etc., *as far as* before that is which he is about to do. But the counsel of the Father is the Word.

*Good.* By which all good things were made. *I speak.* That is, I bring forth the Word: the same here as before; but he says that in that very word are all the works of God; whence: *What was made in him was life,* so that nothing may be in the work which was not first in the counsel. Of this it is said: *God hath spoken once.*

*A pen.* He compares the Word not to sound, which passes away, but to writing, which remains. Or, *swiftly,* because not one thing after another, but all things together in one eternal Word.

*Swiftly.* The power of prophecy, which does not under human torment devise what it divulges to others out of the secret of the Godhead.

*Beautiful in form.* ((CASS.)) He begins the praise of the bridegroom first from his form. *He hath blessed.* The former things the Prophet said in the person of God, these from his own; or all from himself. Or, *he uttereth forth the word,* who says a hymn to God.

*I speak my works.* ((AUG.)) to the praise of him who is from him. *Tongue, a pen.* Because what I say, I also write. Or, *swiftly:* because the things which I write are quickly to come.

((CASS.)) *In the lips.* Because, when he spoke, the world received the grace of reconciliation.
*Gird thyself. ((Ibid.))* Here he praises him from his power; and do thou, being such, *gird thyself.*

*With thy comeliness and beauty. Comeliness* to the humanity, in which he appeared to the world; *beauty* to the Deity, by which he adorns all things.

*Attend.* Pitying, look upon man as he perishes.

*Prosperously.* Setting men free.

*Proceed.* From the womb of the Virgin, as a bridegroom: or, from these conquered to others to be conquered.

*Reign.* Show thy power in the faith of men, thou who hast always reigned. And through this, because both through thyself and through thine own thou teachest the truth, by which thou destroyest our falsehood. And because meek in bearing with the wicked, as when he prayed for his enemies, so also his own: And because he showed the justice of life. And because it shall lead thee on without stumbling through the course of the whole life, or from people to people

*Wonderfully.* Because all shall wonder, or, because he will do miracles.

*The peoples shall fall under thee.* ((AUG.)) That is, many of his enemies shall put themselves under him, and this by reason or by will. This is what the title said: *For those who shall be changed out of the sons of Core.* -- *Into the hearts.* ((CASS.)) Of thy enemies, that they may be friends, as Saul was.

*A throne. ((Ibid.))* Here from judgment: *A throne* pertains to judgment. *A rod. ((Ibid.))* The rule of divine equity, which is truly straight and is never bent: this governs the just, strikes the unjust. ((AUG.)) Let no one presume much to himself concerning mercy, or flatter himself: because the rod of direction, if it governs some, crushes others: it governs the spiritual, it crushes the carnal.

*Thou hast loved. ((Ibid.))* Or, because *thou hast loved justice,* etc., these rewards have been rendered, he made thee king, giving *the name which is above every name.*

*And thou hast hated.* If a man hates iniquity in himself, he acts with God: God hates iniquity, do thou also hate it.

*O God.* ((AUG.)) It is set twice openly in the Greek, the one a vocative, the other a nominative. This one is anointed, that one is the stone which Jacob anointed.

*Myrrh,* etc. ((CASS.)) Here the Prophet praises the bridegroom from his wife and from his adornment; first from the adornment. ((AUG.)) *Myrrh and stacte.* Perfumes are fitly applied to the bridal chamber, etc., *as far as* that is, redemption, through the water of baptism. *Of ivory.* ((HIER.)) In ivory, chastity, which, being dark before, is made bright by saws and files; so the saints, filed down by the cuttings and rubbings of divers punishments, are made bright by the variety of virtues. *The daughters of kings.* ((AUG.)) Of earthly ones, not caring for the honour of their fathers, etc., *as far as* and they took them for the raising up of seed.

*The queen stood,* etc. ((CASS.)) Here he commends the bridegroom from his wife. *With variety. ((Ibid.))* Although there be unity in charity, yet she is adorned with gold, that is, the doctrine of the Apostles, with the scarlet of the martyrs, with the gems of virgins, with the purple of the penitent.

*Hear, O daughter.* ((CASS.)) The praise of the bride is lower, but fourfold: from her form, from her glory, from the maidens, from her offspring. ((AUG.)) *Hear, O daughter.* The Prophet addresses the queen, as one of the fathers. The Jews saw and slew; do thou hear the Gospel, and by believing thou shalt see God: here through an image, in time to come through sight. Or, Hear the prophecies which foretold the incarnation, and see them fulfilled.
*And the king shall desire.* ((CASS.)) Here he praises her from her form.

*Of Tyre.* ((CASS.)) By Tyre, the neighbour of Judaea, the Gentiles are designated; whence the Canaanite woman is a figure of the Church. ((CASS.)) *Of Tyre,* of the Gentiles, the whole from a part. *With gifts.* ((AUG.)) That they may offer themselves, etc., *as far as* the Gentiles, namely, who are in the straits of their sins.

*All the glory.* ((CASS.)) From the glory of the bride, as above from the power of the bridegroom. *From within.* ((AUG.)) Or inwardly. Let almsgiving therefore be in secret, where God sees. Or not in a circumcision made by hand, as in the old law, but in spiritual things. *In fringes.* ((CASS.)) The end of the garment signifies the end of the world or of man. *Golden.* Not gilded, as above, but golden, because in the end is the whole perfection, where charity is found full.

*They shall be brought to the king. ((Ibid.))* Here the bride is praised from her friends, as above from judgment. *((Ibid.)) They shall be brought,* by opportune preaching. *After her. ((Ibid.))* First unity is spoken of, afterward the enumeration of the parts is distinct, when it is said: *Virgins and her neighbours.*

*Instead of thy fathers sons are born to thee. ((Ibid.))* Or in place of the ancient fathers, worshippers of idols, the Apostles were born, princes of preaching. ((AUG.)) Or after the prophets the Apostles, after the Apostles others.

This psalm is sung on the feast of blessed Mary the Virgin, because the things which are here said generally of the Church can be referred specially to Mary. It is sung also for virgins, because it is there said: *Virgins shall be brought to the king.* And for the Apostles, because where it is said: *Sons are born to thee.* Likewise of the nativity of the Lord, because there it treats of the praise of the bridegroom and of the bride and of the nuptials of Christ and the Church, whose espousal was made in the incarnation of the Word.

notes.text: It is impossible the blood of goats should take away sins — Either the guilt or the power of them.

When he cometh into the world — In the fortieth Psalm the Messiah's coming into the world is represented. It is said, into the world, not into the tabernacle, chap. ix, 1; because all the world is interested in his sacrifice. A body hast thou prepared for me - That I may offer up myself. Psalm xl, 6, &c.
In the volume of the book — In this very psalm it is written of me. Accordingly I come to do thy will - By the sacrifice of myself.
Above when he said, Sacrifice thou hast not chosen — That is, when the Psalmist pronounced those words in his name.

Then said he — in that very instant he subjoined. Lo, I come to do Thy will - To offer a more acceptable sacrifice; and by this very act he taketh away the legal, that he may establish the evangelical, dispensation.
By which will — Of God, done and suffered by Christ. We are sanctified - Cleansed from guilt, and consecrated to God.

glossa.text: *Thou wouldst not.* From the time of the passion, in which is the consummation of all victims, those things began to displease. He never destroyed them before, but was subject to them, when he was presented in the temple with victims. *But a body thou hast fitted to me.* The signs are taken away, because the truth has been shown forth, then was the time that those should be taken away, and the truth should come. Nor was the Lord ever delighted in those odours, save in the faith and the desire of him that offered. Yet he commanded these things to be offered to himself, rather than that they should be offered to idols; and he imposed them for servitude, not for justification, and that they might be a figure of what was to come.

*They have not pleased.* In those figures the truth was foretold. They celebrate figures, many knowing the thing of the figure, but more not knowing it, which figures must cease when the thing has been shown forth.

*Then.* When I saw that all those things displeased, and that a body fit for this was given to me. *I said: Behold I come,* to offer myself, that I may do and fulfil thy will, because thou art my God. Therefore I come to fulfil thy thy will, because so it is written, and prefigured concerning me in the counsel of the Godhead, which is my head, I who am the book of the human race according as I am man, in which book let men read all things necessary for them, and therefore there is no need of the law.

*Saying above.* As if he should say: This authority notes not only that the old victims did not make men perfect, but that the victim of Christ alone did; but also the taking away of the Old Testament, and the establishing of the New, if the words be diligently noted; because, saying above, *thou wouldst not have those things,* he adds: *Then I said.* For behold, he takes away the first sacrifice and with it the Old Testament, and appoints as stable the new sacrifice and with it the New Testament.
*Sanctified,* etc. The purgation of sins having been made, we are reconciled to God.

notes.text: In the sixth month — After Elisabeth had conceived.

Espoused — It was customary among the Jews, for persons that married to contract before witnesses some time before. And as Christ was to be born of a pure virgin, so the wisdom of God ordered it to be of one espoused, that to prevent reproach he might have a reputed father, according to the flesh.

Hail, thou highly favoured; the Lord is with thee; blessed art thou among women — Hail is the salutation used by our Lord to the women after his resurrection: thou art highly favoured, or hast found favour with God, ver. 30, is no more than was said of Noah, Moses, and David. The Lord is with thee, was said to Gideon, Judg. vi, 12; and blessed shall she be above women, of Jael, Judg. v, 24. This salutation gives no room for any pretense of paying adoration to the virgin; as having no appearance of a prayer, or of worship offered to her.

He shall be called the Son of the Highest — In this respect also: and that in a more eminent sense than any, either man or angel, can be called so. The Lord shall give him the throne of his father David - That is, the spiritual kingdom, of which David's was a type.
He shall reign over the house of Jacob — In which all true believers are included.

The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee — The power of God was put forth by the Holy Ghost, as the immediate Divine agent in this work: and so he exerted the power of the Highest as his own power, who together with the Father and the Son is the most high God. Therefore also - Not only as he is God from eternity, but on this account likewise he shall be called the Son of God.

And behold, thy cousin Elisabeth — Though Elisabeth was of the house of Aaron, and Mary of the house of David, by the fathers side, they might be related by their mothers. For the law only forbad heiresses marrying into another tribe. And so other persons continually intermarried; particularly the families of David and of Levi.
And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord — It is not improbable, that this time of the virgin's humble faith, consent, and expectation, might be the very time of her conceiving.

glossa.text:
*And in the sixth month. ((HIER.))* As in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God into a city of Galilee, so in the sixth millennium Christ was sent,

*Gabriel. ((BEDA.))* For this reason angels are sometimes marked out by a name, so that from the name itself it may be shown what they come to minister. Gabriel is the strength of God, because he announces him who was coming to war down the devil.
*To a virgin.* A woman seduced by the devil brought in death: on the contrary, a woman taught by an angel brought forth salvation.

*The Lord is with thee.* Whom by a new love of chastity he raised up to heavenly things, and afterwards, human nature mediating, consecrated with all the fullness of the Godhead. *Blessed art thou among women.* Who, without example in the condition of women, is both virgin and mother, and brought forth God.
*She was troubled,* etc. Because she did not know whether what the angel said was past or to come.

*And the angel said to her: Fear not, Mary.* Her, troubled by the unwonted salutation, he calls by name as one more familiarly known. He bids her not to fear, and more fully explains why he had called her full of grace.

*Jesus.* Jesus is called saviour, or salutary. For he himself shall save, not the people of Israel, but his own people, whether from the uncircumcision or from the circumcision, gathered into one fold under one shepherd.
*The throne of David his father. ((BEDA.))* That is, the Israelite people, etc., *as far as* in those who, cut from the wild olive, have been grafted into the good olive.

*The Holy One shall be called the Son of God.* Jesus is born holy, who was to overcome the condition of corruptible nature, and he was not conceived by the mingling of carnal union. We, bound fast by the condition of corruptible nature, can be sanctified through grace. And it is fitting that she who conceived as a virgin against custom should bring forth the Son of God above the custom of human usage.

*And behold,* etc. ((BEDA.)) Lest the virgin should despair of the childbearing, etc., *as far as* she might know that the forerunner too was to be born of a barren old woman.

*Thy cousin.* Because she was of the tribe of Levi, that is, of the tribe of God.

((BEDA.)) We read that Aaron, who was of the tribe of Levi, etc., *as far as* which according to God did not lack the fellowship of a spiritual kinship.

*Behold the handmaid of the Lord.* She does not exalt herself for the singularity of her merit, but, mindful in all things of her own condition and of the divine kinship, she confesses herself to be the handmaid of him whose mother she is chosen to be, and with great devotion desires the angel's promise to be fulfilled.

events.label: The Syro-Ephraimite war
events.note: Pekah of Israel and Rezin of Aram march on Jerusalem to force Judah into their coalition against Assyria. Ahaz buys Tiglath-Pileser III instead, who strips Galilee. To Ahaz, Isaiah gives the sign of Immanuel.

echoes.text: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
echoes.note: A 'virgin' (parthenos) of the house of David who will 'conceive... and give birth to a son' and name him directly evokes Isaiah 7:13-14 (LXX), 'the virgin shall conceive and bear a son.' The house-of-David setting plus virgin + conceive + bear + name a son yields high volume and is the controlling messianic citation.

echoes.text: “Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
echoes.note: 'Blessed are you among women' quotes the blessing of Jael, 'Most blessed of women be Jael' (Judges 5:24). The exact superlative-blessing-of-a-woman formula gives high volume; it recurs on Elizabeth's lips at 1:42.

echoes.text: Ozias said to her, “Blessed are you, daughter, in the sight of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth; and blessed is the Lord God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to cut off the head of the prince of our enemies.
echoes.note: Uzziah blesses Judith, 'Blessed are you... above all women on earth' (Judith 13:18), the closest verbal and contextual parallel to the angel/Elizabeth's beatitude over Mary. A deuterocanonical text celebrating a woman through whom God delivers Israel; high distinctiveness.

echoes.text: When your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men; but my loving kindness shall not […]
echoes.note: 'The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign... forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom' is built on the Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7:12-16, where God establishes David's offspring and 'his throne forever.' High volume (throne, forever, kingdom, father David) and the foundational role of Nathan's oracle make this the primary source.

echoes.text: For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on the throne of David, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.
echoes.note: 'The throne of his father David... no end to his Kingdom' closely echoes Isaiah 9:7, 'of the increase of his government and of peace there will be no end, on the throne of David.' The 'no end' phrase is distinctive and reinforces the messianic-throne reading alongside 2 Samuel 7.

echoes.text: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my servant, ‘I will establish your seed forever, and build up your throne to all generations.’” Selah.
echoes.note: The everlasting Davidic throne is celebrated in Psalm 89:3-4,29,36, 'I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.' Recurrence of the throne-forever covenant language across this Psalm supports the high-volume Davidic cluster here.

echoes.text: yes, while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering.
echoes.note: 'The angel Gabriel was sent from God' continues the Danielic Gabriel motif (Daniel 8:16; 9:21), where the same angel is 'sent' to deliver revelation. Recurrence within the chapter, more than fresh volume here, secures the allusion.

echoes.text: Sing, daughter of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. Yahweh has taken away your judgments. He has thrown out your enemy. The King of Israel, Yahweh, is in your midst. You will not be afraid of evil any more. In that day, it will be said to Jerusalem, “Don’t be afraid, Zion. Don’t let your hands be weak.” Yahweh, your God, is in your midst, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He […]
echoes.note: 'Rejoice (chaire)... the Lord is with you' echoes the address to Daughter Zion: 'Rejoice, O Daughter of Zion... the Lord your God is in your midst' (Zephaniah 3:14-17 LXX). The greeting-rejoice + indwelling-Lord pairing casts Mary figurally as Zion; volume is moderate but coherence strong.

echoes.text: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
echoes.note: 'Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion' announcing the coming king (Zechariah 9:9) is a second Daughter-Zion 'rejoice' source standing behind Gabriel's chaire. The royal-advent context coheres with the Davidic throne promise that follows; the link competes with Zephaniah 3 and is thus contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s angel appeared to him, and said to him, “Yahweh is with you, you mighty man of valor!”
echoes.note: 'The Lord is with you' reproduces the angel's salutation to Gideon, 'The Lord is with you, mighty man of valor' (Judges 6:12), within a near-identical commissioning-of-a-deliverer scene including a 'how can this be' objection. The shared formula and scene-type give a coherent allusion.

echoes.text: But Noah found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.
echoes.note: 'You have found favor with God' uses the Septuagintal idiom of Noah, who 'found favor in the eyes of the Lord' (Genesis 6:8; cf. Exodus 33:17 of Moses). The found-favor formula marks Mary as a chosen recipient of divine grace in the line of Israel's elect.

echoes.text: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: 'There will be no end to his Kingdom' resonates with the Son of Man's 'everlasting dominion which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed' (Daniel 7:14). The everlasting, indestructible kingdom motif coheres with the Danielic frame already established by Gabriel.

echoes.text: and I will make that which was lame a remnant, and that which was cast far off a strong nation: and Yahweh will reign over them on Mount Zion from then on, even forever.”
echoes.note: 'He will reign over the house of Jacob forever' faintly echoes 'the Lord will reign over them in Mount Zion... forever' (Micah 4:7). The everlasting-reign-over-restored-Israel idea coheres, but the diction is generic and the Davidic sources above are nearer, so this is a low, contested echo.

echoes.text: Moses wasn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle.
echoes.note: 'The power of the Most High will overshadow (episkiasei) you' uses the verb for the glory-cloud that 'overshadowed' the tent of meeting when the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35 LXX). The distinctive Shekinah-overshadowing diction frames Mary as the dwelling place of God's presence; high volume.

echoes.text: Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes round, and Sarah will have a son.”
echoes.note: 'For everything spoken by God is possible' answers the rhetorical question to Abraham and Sarah, 'Is anything too hard (impossible, LXX) for the Lord?' (Genesis 18:14), in the very context of a miraculous conception by an old, barren woman. The verbal and situational match is high-volume and pointed.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: 'The Holy Spirit will come on you' may echo the Spirit of God hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2), framing the conception as a new creative act. Thematic coherence is suggestive but verbal overlap is thin, so the link is a contested creation-echo.

echoes.text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
echoes.note: 'The holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God' draws on the Davidic adoption formula, 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son' (2 Samuel 7:14). Coheres tightly with the throne-of-David promise of 1:32-33, extending the Nathan-oracle source.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: 'Son of God' applied to the messianic king recalls 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you' (Psalm 2:7). The royal son-of-God theme coheres, but the title is mediated through 2 Samuel 7 and is conventional, so Psalm 2 is a contested secondary echo.

echoes.text: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
echoes.note: 'Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren' replays the Sarah situation of Genesis 18:11 and the impossible-birth promise. Recurrence of the aged-barren-woman motif (cf. 1:7) sets up the 'nothing impossible' declaration that follows.

echoes.text: Ah Lord Yahweh! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm; there is nothing too hard for you,
echoes.note: 'Nothing will be impossible with God' also echoes Jeremiah 32:17,27, 'Ah, Lord God!... nothing is too hard for you... is anything too hard for me?' The omnipotence formula reinforces the Genesis 18 source with a prophetic doublet.

echoes.text: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
echoes.note: Job's confession, 'I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted' (Job 42:2 LXX), is a further scriptural articulation of the impossibility-with-God theme Gabriel invokes. A coherent supporting echo of divine omnipotence.

echoes.text: She vowed a vow, and said, “Yahweh of Armies, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your handmaid, and remember me, and not forget your handmaid, but will give to your handmaid a boy, then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
echoes.note: 'Behold, the handmaid (doule) of the Lord' takes up Hannah's self-designation as 'your handmaid' before the Lord (1 Samuel 1:11). The humble servant-woman posture coheres with the Hannah/Magnificat substratum that crystallizes a few verses later.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The Lord himself gives a sign: a young woman shall bear a son.
And they shall call his name Immanuel, God with us.
Greetings, favored one; the Lord is with you.
Let it be to us according to your word.
A body you have prepared; behold, I have come to do your will.
Nothing will be impossible with God.
Come, let us worship the Word made flesh.
Our souls magnify the Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture an ordinary room, an ordinary girl, and then the air bright with an angel, and the words: greetings, favored one.
Let it be to us according to your word.
She was troubled, and afraid, and asked how this could be; and the answer was the Spirit, the power of the Most High overshadowing her.
Let it be to us according to your word.
This is the sign Isaiah promised: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name will be God-with-us.
Let it be to us according to your word.
For a body has been prepared, and the eternal Word says, behold, I have come to do your will, O God.
Let it be to us according to your word.
Nothing is impossible with God; what he speaks, he does. Come, let us worship the Word made flesh.
Let it be to us according to your word. Our souls magnify the Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The angel comes to an ordinary room: greetings, favored one.
Let it be to us according to your word.
A virgin shall bear a son, and call him Immanuel.
Let it be to us according to your word.
Behold, I have come to do your will, O God.
Let it be to us according to your word.
Come, let us worship the Word made flesh.
Let it be to us according to your word. Amen.
